title: Classical simulation of polynomial-gap local stoquastic adiabatic computation
formal: Can every polynomial-time adiabatic computation described by explicit local stoquastic Hamiltonians with an inverse-polynomial global spectral gap be sampled classically in polynomial time to inverse-polynomial total-variation error?
definitions: A Hamiltonian is stoquastic in the computational basis when every off-diagonal matrix entry is real and nonpositive. The intended input describes a smoothly varying sum of terms acting on a constant number of qubits, an efficiently preparable initial ground state and computational-basis measurement at the end. The gap is the separation of the lowest two eigenvalues of the full Hamiltonian, not only a symmetry-restricted subspace. The intended simulator is uniform randomized classical computation.

context_blocks.text: Stoquasticity removes a sign obstruction that often complicates classical statistical simulation. Whether that suffices for efficient simulation of general explicit local adiabatic computations remains a basic question about the source of quantum computational power.

Bringewatt and Jarret study obstructions based on symmetry sectors and obtain subexponential simulations for those examples. Their result does not establish a general polynomial-time simulation theorem. Oracle-model separations also require care before being transferred to explicitly supplied local interactions.

why: Determine the computational power of a central restricted adiabatic model.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
